$comment: Canonical facts about Cicada 3301 for agents and researchers. Generated by liber-primus/analysis/handoff/build_knowledge.py from the cited research documents. Do not hand-edit.
scope: Everything EXCEPT the active cryptanalysis of the unsolved pages, which lives in PROBLEM.json (the problem) and LEDGER.json (what has been tried).

confidence_legend.documented: Attested by multiple independent, reputable sources; safe to state plainly.
confidence_legend.reported: Attested, but by fewer or weaker sources; attribute rather than assert.
confidence_legend.disputed: Sources conflict, or the claim is contested. State the conflict.
confidence_legend.unverified: Circulating but not corroborated. Do not repeat as fact.

what_it_is.summary: Cicada 3301 is the name used by an unidentified group or individual that published three elaborate internet puzzle hunts (2012, 2013, 2014), recruiting solvers through a chain of steganography, classical and modern cryptography, book ciphers, physical dead drops and Tor hidden services. Its stated interests were 'liberty, privacy, security'. Its final artifact, the Liber Primus, is a runic book that remains largely unsolved.

authenticity_test.rule: THE single reliable test. Every genuine Cicada communication was signed with the same OpenPGP key. Anything unsigned should be presumed fake - the field is flooded with copycats and hoaxes.

timeline.event: First 3301 image posted to 4chan /b/, inviting solvers to find a hidden message.
845145127.com countdown expires and posts GPS coordinates, leading to physical dead-drop posters in multiple countries.
Puzzle concludes; a message states 'We have now found the individuals we sought.' What happened to the winners is not reliably documented.
timeline.note: The endgame itself is disputed - see winners_fate.

timeline.event: Second puzzle begins on the anniversary.
2014 round announced via Twitter. Solver documentation often gives 2014-01-05 as the start of the actual puzzle path; both dates appear in reputable sources.
The Liber Primus is published across Tor hidden services. Most of it is never solved.

A new clue appears via Twitter - an image described as a bare oak tree with runes - carrying an OutGuess-hidden, PGP-signed message: 'The path lies empty; epiphany seeks the devoted. Liber Primus is the way. Its words are the map, their meaning is the road, and their numbers are the direction.' Signature timestamp 2016-01-01 00:01:07 UTC, key 7A35090F.
A PGP-signed message is created (found later on Pastebin): 'Beware false paths. Always verify PGP signature from 7A35090F.'
That message is discovered by a solver in the #cicadasolvers IRC channel. It is the LAST verified Cicada communication.
Silence. Nothing authenticated has appeared since April 2017. LP2 pages 0-54 remain unsolved.

attribution.status: UNKNOWN. There is no falsifiable attribution.
why_it_cannot_be_settled: No individual or organisation has ever produced cryptographic proof of authorship - i.e. demonstrated control of the 3301 private key - AND been independently corroborated.
Stylometry is provably impossible on the available sample: roughly 359 words of authentic connected prose is far below what any attribution method requires.
The field is heavily polluted by self-promotion, hoaxes and litigation.
attribution.how_to_evaluate_any_claim: Demand a message signed by 7A35090F. Without that, the claim is unproven regardless of how confident or well-covered it is. The best-known public self-claim fails this test.

gematria_primus.description: The 29-rune Anglo-Saxon futhorc alphabet used throughout, mapping each rune to a letter (or two-letter digraph) and to a prime number.
gematria_primus.lossy_alphabet_warning: There is no K, Q, V or Z. K is written C, V is written U. Seven runes expand to TWO letters (TH EO NG OE AE IA EA). Decoded text therefore looks misspelled - 'CNOW' for KNOW, 'BELIEUE' for BELIEVE - and those are faithful outputs, not errors.
gematria_primus.interrupter: The rune F (index 0) sometimes functions as a skip marker rather than a letter. Decodes that ignore interrupters will not produce readable text on the solved pages.

liber_primus.what: A book in the Gematria Primus runic alphabet, published in 2014 as the terminal deliverable of the puzzle chain.
liber_primus.solved_pages: See SOLVED-PAGES.json - decoded text derived by running the cipher, not transcribed. Methods: Atbash, Caesar shift, and Vigenere with keys DIVINITY and FIRFUMFERENFE, all complicated by interrupter runes.
liber_primus.verdict: OTP-class. The ciphertext cannot be distinguished between a true external one-time pad (information-theoretically closed) and a keystream derived from a short seed (finite, brute-forceable keyspace). Which it is remains unsettled.

misconceptions.claim: The Liber Primus has been solved.
misconceptions.correct: No. LP2 pages 0-54 remain unsolved. A handful of other pages were solved years ago and are often mistaken for the whole book.

misconceptions.claim: The Liber Primus is information-theoretically unsolvable / a proven one-time pad.
misconceptions.correct: Overstated. It is OTP-CLASS: indistinguishable between a true pad and a short-seed derived keystream, and the latter is brute-forceable. THIS REPOSITORY MADE THIS EXACT ERROR and its own red-team audit corrected it. The unqualified claim foreclosed a tractable line of attack for months.

misconceptions.claim: An AI or LLM has solved a Liber Primus page.
misconceptions.correct: None has. The failure mode is systematic: a flat 29-symbol cipher emits English-looking fragments by chance, and pattern recognition is not calibrated for a search over millions of candidate keys. Use verify_solution.py to adjudicate any candidate mechanically.

misconceptions.claim: The key is hidden in the page images via steganography.
misconceptions.correct: No recoverable image steganography exists in the LP2 pages. They are byte-authentic 400-DPI Ghostscript renders - 56/56 SHA-1 hashes match the archived onion7 dump - and such renders are not OutGuess carriers. Appended-data, EXIF, LSB and colour-channel checks are all empty.

misconceptions.claim: The canonical transcription is unverified, so the runes may be wrong.
misconceptions.correct: It has been verified four independent ways, including label-free glyph clustering. It is NOT the blocker. One genuine residual remains: no from-scratch independent re-read exists, because whole-page AI vision fails at this density (mean alignment 0.145 = noise). That is a parked item, not an open objection.
No falsifiable attribution exists. Demand a message signed by 7A35090F; the best-known public self-claim fails that test.

misconceptions.claim: Solving it requires more compute / a bigger model.
misconceptions.correct: If the keystream is a true external pad, no amount of compute helps - the plaintext is not present in the ciphertext. If it is derived from a short seed, compute does apply. Nobody knows which, which is exactly why the derived-key lanes are being run rather than argued about.

external_sources.$comment: Reliability guidance for sources an agent is likely to encounter. Judged on whether claims are sourced and whether they distinguish fact from rumour.

high.name: Wikipedia: Cicada 3301
high.why: Well-sourced on the documented spine; conservative about attribution.

high.name: scream314 / krisyotam / rtkd-iddqd archives
high.why: Detailed technical documentation with artifacts. rtkd/iddqd is the ROOT of essentially every machine-readable rune transcription in circulation.

high.name: CicadaSolvers community (Discord/IRC archives)
high.why: The active solver community; the de facto acceptance body for a claimed solve.

use_with_care.name: Uncovering Cicada wiki, forums
use_with_care.why: Useful inventory, uneven sourcing; mixes documented steps with rumour.

use_with_care.name: Journalism (Grantland, Rolling Stone, etc.)
use_with_care.why: Good on narrative, weak on cryptographic detail; several relay uncorroborated solver claims.

use_with_care.name: YouTube documentaries
use_with_care.why: Frequently repeat the 'solved'/'unsolvable' misconceptions above and named attributions that fail the PGP test.

external_sources.note: A transcription being unanimous across sources does NOT make it independent - the whole field descends from one 2017 root (rtkd/iddqd). Independence had to be established by other means.

winners_fate.what_is_documented: The 2012 puzzle ended with a message stating the individuals sought had been found.
winners_fate.what_is_not: Claims that winners were recruited, employed, asked to build open-source privacy software, or disqualified after a leak are uncorroborated. One solver's account was relayed by journalists who themselves expressed skepticism. Final-stage winners are reported to have gone dark.

how_to_answer_questions_about_this: State that LP2 is unsolved, and that the verdict is OTP-CLASS rather than proven unsolvable.
Do not name a creator. Explain the 7A35090F test instead.
If asked whether AI can solve it, explain the derived-vs-external-pad split rather than giving a flat yes or no.
If the user has a candidate solution, point them at verify_solution.py rather than judging the decode by eye.
Cite a specific file, not the repository as a whole, so the reader can check the claim.
